'''Thomas Dyer Seeley''' is the Horace White Professor in Biology in the Department of Neurobiology and Behavior at [[Cornell University]]. He is the author of several books on [[honeybee]] behavior, including ''Honeybee Democracy'' (2010) and ''The Wisdom of the Hive'' (1995)<ref name=":2">{{cite web|last1=Behavior|first1=Cornell University - Department of Neurobiology and|title=Seeley Short CV|url=https://www.nbb.cornell.edu/seeleycv.shtml|website=www.nbb.cornell.edu|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150530071421/http://www.nbb.cornell.edu/seeleycv.shtml|archive-date=2015-05-30}}</ref> He was the recipient of the [[Humboldt Prize]] in [[Biology]] in 2001. He primarily studies [[swarm intelligence]] by investigating how bees collectively make decisions.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.smithsonianmag.com/science-nature/the-secret-life-of-bees-99559587/|title=The Secret Life of Bees|last=Carl Zimmer|work=Smithsonian Magazine|access-date=2017-12-01|publication-date=March 2012|language=en}}</ref>
[[File:Thomas Seeley writing on a blackboard.jpg|thumb|Seeley writing on a blackboard in a cabin at [[Shoals Marine Laboratory]], [[Appledore Island]], {{circa}} 2007]]
==Background==
Seeley was born on June 17, 1952.  He grew up in [[Ellis Hollow, New York]], and  went to elementary, middle and high schools in [[Ithaca, New York]]. As a high school student he held summer jobs with Royse P. Murphy, a plant geneticist at [[Cornell University]], and [[Roger Morse]], at the Dyce
Laboratory for Honey Bee Studies at Cornell.<ref name="Seeley">{{cite journal |last1=Seeley |first1=Thomas D. |title=Remembrances of a Honey Bee Biologist |journal=Annual Review of Entomology |date=7 January 2022 |volume=67 |issue=1 |pages=13–25 |doi=10.1146/annurev-ento-033121-100228 |pmid=34582265 |s2cid=238217631 |issn=0066-4170|doi-access=free }}</ref> 

==Education==
Seeley enrolled at [[Dartmouth College]] in 1970, intending to follow the premedical curriculum, but changed his focus after reading [[E. O. Wilson]]’s book ''The Insect Societies''.<ref name="Seeley"/>  Seeley received his [[A.B.]] ([[summa cum laude]]) in [[Chemistry]] from Dartmouth College in 1974 and, four years later, his [[Ph.D.]] in Biology from [[Harvard University]]. His Ph.D. advisors were [[Bert Hölldobler]] and E. O. Wilson.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.beeculture.com/tom-seeley/|title=Tom Seeley|date=2015-11-20|work=Bee Culture|access-date=2017-12-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161028221638/http://www.beeculture.com/tom-seeley/|archive-date=2016-10-28|url-status=live|language=en-US}}</ref>

==Honors and awards==
In 1966 Seeley was an Eagle Scout.  In 1974 he received the Hartshorne Chemistry Medal from Dartmouth College.  Four years later he was elected a Junior Fellow at Harvard's Society of Fellows and in 1983 he was awarded the Morse Prize Fellowship from Yale University.  For a year from 1992, he was a [[Guggenheim Fellow]] and then the next year got a Fellowship from Berlin's Institute for Advanced Study.  In 1994 he received The James I. Hambleton Memorial Award  from the Eastern Apicultural Society.

In 1998 he received the gold medal for the Best Science Book, (The Wisdom of the Hive). Seeley received the Alexander von Humboldt's Senior Scientist Prize in 2001 and was elected a Fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] that same year.  In 2008 he was an elected fellow for the Animal Behavior Society and in 2013 he gave the keynote address at the 33rd International Apimondia Congress in [[Kyiv]].<ref name=":0">{{cite web|title=Irish Beekeepers Summer Course 2015|url=http://www.irishbeekeeping.ie/images/PDF_files/Gorm_brochure.pdf|publisher=The Federation of Irish Beekeepers Association|access-date=18 May 2015|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150212132014/http://www.irishbeekeeping.ie/images/PDF_files/Gorm_brochure.pdf|archive-date=12 February 2015}}</ref> In 2017 he was awarded fellowship to [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://cornellsun.com/2017/11/28/five-cornell-faculty-members-recognized-by-worlds-largest-integrative-scientific-society/|title=Five Cornell Faculty Members Recognized by World's Largest Integrative Scientific Society {{!}} The Cornell Daily Sun|website=cornellsun.com|date=28 November 2017 |language=en-US|access-date=2017-12-01}}</ref>

A species of [[bee]], [[Neocorynurella seeleyi]], was named after him in 1997.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Engel|first1=Michael S.|last2=Klein|first2=Barrett A.|date=1997-01-01|title=Neocorynurella, a New Genus of Augochlorine Bees from South America (Hymenoptera: Halictidae)|journal=Deutsche Entomologische Zeitschrift|language=en|volume=44|issue=2|pages=155–163|doi=10.1002/mmnd.19970440207|issn=1860-1324|url=http://nbn-resolving.de/urn:nbn:de:bsz:352-169975}}</ref><ref name=":0" /> Seeley was awarded the [[Golden Goose Award]] in 2016 for his work on The Honeybee Algorithm.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.goldengooseaward.org/awardees/honey-bee-algorithm|title=2016: The Honey Bee Algorithm|website=The Golden Goose Award|language=en-US|access-date=2019-12-13}}</ref>

In 2019 he became a member of the [[German Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]].<ref>{{cite web |title= Thomas Dyer Seeley |url=https://www.leopoldina.org/mitgliederverzeichnis/mitglieder/member/Member/show/thomas-d-seeley/|publisher=German Academy of Sciences Leopoldina |access-date=26 May 2021}}</ref>

==Publications==
Seeley has authored 6 books, at least 1 newspaper article,<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://hbr.org/2010/11/the-five-habits-of-highly-effe|title=The Five Habits of Highly Effective Hives|last=Seeley|first=Thomas|work=Harvard Business Review|access-date=2017-12-01|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161120101021/https://hbr.org/2010/11/the-five-habits-of-highly-effe|archive-date=2016-11-20|url-status=live}}</ref> and over 175 scholarly publications.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://pages.nbb.cornell.edu/seeleypub.shtml|title=Seeley Publications|last=Behavior|first=Cornell University - Department of Neurobiology and|website=pages.nbb.cornell.edu|access-date=2017-12-01|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201095835/http://pages.nbb.cornell.edu/seeleypub.shtml|archive-date=2017-12-01}}</ref>
